title: Signal-fusion Gating for Automatic Region/Tier Model Fallbacks
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Implement a unified signal-fusion gate that automatically triggers region/tier fallback and model-variant circuit breakers when composite failure signals (429 rate, request timeouts, 5xx error spikes, and upstream saturation) exceed context-aware thresholds. The gate must support distinct policies per customer tier (hosted free, hosted paid, dedicated), per-region hysteresis, and per-route sensitivity to preserve SLOs while minimizing unnecessary failovers.
background: We currently have multiple experiments and tickets that touch fallback behavior: per-tenant probation (ENG-163901), regional handover heuristics (ENG-48210), and trip-score decay (ENG-116512). However, there is no single component that consolidates signals and makes unified decisions across region, tier, and model variant. This causes inconsistent behavior during bursts and complicates observability and postmortems.
proposed_solution: Build a Signal Fusion Gate (SFG) service that consumes standardized failure signals (429s, timeout counts, 5xx ratios, queue-length-derived saturation) and computes a composite trip score. The SFG exposes a small decision API used by the routing layer: SHOULD_FAILOVER(region,tier,route,tenant) -> {action: no-op|soft-degrade|failover|isolate}. Policies are declarative YAML with adjustable weights, hysteresis windows, and decay rates. The SFG must be able to: 1) apply tenant overrides, 2) respect dedicated-pool invariants, 3) return explainability metadata for audits.
design_decisions: 1) Composite scoring: weighted sum of z-scored metrics to keep thresholds model-agnostic. 2) Hysteresis: require sustained trip_score > high_threshold for 30s before hard failover; allow soft-degrade at lower_threshold for 5s. 3) Decay: exponential decay with half-life per-policy (default 60s) to avoid flapping. 4) Per-tenant probation window after automated recovery (default 10m) to prevent immediate re-attach. 5) Granularity: compute signals at route+region+tier and aggregate to region-level when authoritative. 6) Fallback ordering: prefer cheaper compatible model variant in same region, then cross-region warm fallback, then tenant-specific Dedicated fallback only if allowed. 7) Observability: every decision must emit a structured event with contributing signals and versioned policy id.
telemetry_metrics: failover_actions.count - counter (labels: action, tenant, region, route)
acceptance_criteria: SFG deployed behind feature flag; routing layer calls SHOULD_FAILOVER and honors responses
Policy YAML supports per-tenant and per-tier overrides and can be reloaded without restart
Composite trip score reproducible in tests using recorded signals
Failover decision emits structured event with signals and policy_id
Integration test that injects 429/timeouts causes soft-degrade then hard failover within configured windows
Dashboard tile showing trip_score and failovers per region is live in Console staging
No increase in tail latency for unaffected routes (>99th percentile unchanged within 1%) after enabling SFG

Implement SFG core scoring engine (Go service) - Akash

Create migration plan for existing experiments to use policy IDs - PM

Run canary on internal traffic then 1% external traffic before full rollout - SRE
risks: False positives: aggressive thresholds could cause unnecessary failovers and degraded quality
New single point of decisioning: SFG outages must be gracefully degraded to default routing behavior
Policy complexity: many per-tenant overrides increase surface area for misconfiguration
Observability gaps: insufficient signal instrumentation will cause opaque decisions
Cross-region failovers may violate data residency for some tenants
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged SFG in staging; 24h soak with chaos-induced 429/timeouts
Expand to 1% of customer traffic with monitoring alerts for false-positive failovers
Enable per-tenant opt-in for dedicated customers for first month
Gradual ramp to 100% with weekly policy audits and two-week probation for recovered tenants
notes: We will reuse normalized signal exporters from runtime-telemetry to avoid duplication
Default policy will be conservative for hosted free tier and more aggressive for Dedicated (because of isolation guarantees)
SFG API latency target: <5ms median, 95th <20ms under normal load; timeout at routing layer: 50ms
Auth: routing queries use signed tokens tied to policy-read role; decisions are cached for 500ms per route to reduce RPC load
